player.seasonOutlook: The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Johnson paced New Orleans' tight ends in yards (53) during the Week 1 overtime loss but trailed Noah Fant in receptions (three to four) and targets (seven to eight). Despite this, Johnson was on the field for 72 of the Saints' 90 offensive snaps, where Fant played just 37. Thus, Johnson is expected to remain New Orleans' top TE option against a Ravens defense that allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points to the position in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Johnson had another productive outing in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, catching six of eight targets for 59 yards. He's now tallied 232 receiving yards through four contests this season, the fourth-most amongst tight ends. Johnson will likely continue to benefit from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense that's averaged 45 pass attempts per game this year. Despite this, Johnson is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Bell hopes for additional volume in the Dolphins Week 2 matchup at San Francisco. Coming off an ACL tear in November, the rookie logged a 52.7% snap share in his NFL debut, ending with a 25-yard catch on two targets. Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas dominated the targets in Miami's limited passing game, as expected given their availability throughout training camp. The 49ers' secondary doesn't appear to be one where Bell can break out, allowing just 6.4 yards per target in Week 1. Bell is worth monitoring, but he's currently off the fantasy radar.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Bell will hope to build on his best game of his rookie season in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. Bell posted seven targets in Week 3 after just three in the first two weeks, playing 72% of offensive snaps with Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined. Bell is the Dolphins' highest-ceiling option, but the passing game hasn't thrived under Malik Willis. Likely playing from behind, Bell could excel against a secondary that has misleading stats thanks to a Week 2 monsoon in Chicago that shut down the passing game, but Bell needs to turn potential into production before earning fantasy trust.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Bell is failing to gain traction in the Dolphins' limited passing attack ahead of a Week 5 tilt with the Bengals. Bell failed to record a catch on three targets in Week 4 in a game where Miami threw only 17 times, completing nine of them. Bell remains long on potential, but he's garnered three or fewer looks in three of Miami's first four games, and a breakout against a middling Bengals defense that hasn't allowed more than 63 yards to an opposing receiver seems unlikely.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik Willis plays well, but there are enough concerns that he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Reichard converted his lone field-goal attempt and four PATs in a come-from-behind Week 1 win over Green Bay. The third-year kicker was only on the field for extra-point tries after nailing a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the nature of the game made Minnesota more ambitious with their offensive scheme. This could give Reichard more opportunities against a Chicago defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack seven points to Ryan Fitzgerald this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Reichard will look to stay hot as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Reichard converted all three of his field-goal attempts in a bad-weather win over the Bears in Week 2. The third-year kicker has now nailed four field goals and all four of his PATs this year. He'll face a Bucs squad that's tied for the most fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (13.0) so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Reichard finished with his best game of the season in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts (including two 50-plus-yarders) and knocking in two extra-point tries. The third-year kicker will now focus on a Miami team that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 6.7 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Reichard should be a high-volume option once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 4 against the Dolphins, scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points from field goals. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last three games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Saints squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against kickers this season,

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Herbert struggled in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards and one touchdown with one interception, while adding 29 rushing yards on five carries. Injuries along the offensive line were once again an issue for the club; the interior of the line, with rookie Jake Slaughter at center, wasn't able to hold up, and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel didn't seem to have many answers. Ladd McConkey also suffered a rib injury in the game, which could make things even more difficult for Herbert if the top wideout misses any time. Herbert will look to rebound in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season with Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator. Through two games, he's completed less than 60% of his passes with a 2:3 TD:INT ratio and barely over 200 passing yards per game. Ladd McConkey was his only reliable target in the Chargers' opener, but the third-year wideout was limited by a rib injury in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and no one else stepped up. As in years past, Herbert's protection has also been decimated by injuries. An offensive line that was already missing starting center Tyler Biadasz was down to a third-string left guard against Las Vegas in Week 2, and the team also lost its two best blocking tight ends, Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, over the course of that contest. Herbert could be in for another long day in Week 3 against a Bills defense that has seven sacks through two games, tied for fourth in the league, but which has been vulnerable through the air when the opposing QB has found some time.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The veteran quarterback has yet to throw multiple touchdowns in a game this season, while his 59.1% completion rate would be a career-worst mark. Herbert is also dealing with his usual protection issues and has been sacked eight times in three contests, a pace that would see him get brought down more than 40 times for a third straight year. His top target, Ladd McConkey, should be healthier as he puts a rib injury further behind him, but as yet none of his other pass catchers have made any kind of impact. Herbert's rough year could get worse in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 28-year-old quarterback posted season lows with 189 passing yards and 6.1 yards per attempt in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. Through four games, he has a career-low 59.7% completion rate and a weak 4:6 TD:INT. An ineffective running game, along with injuries to the offensive line and his wide receiver corps, have contributed to the team's 0-4 start, but Herbert has been the focal point of the offense's woes. He'll try to turn things around in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain, and which ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Herbert enters his seventh NFL season following a solid 2025 campaign in which he ranked just inside the top 10 quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns. Herbert added serious value with his legs, ranking fifth at the position in carries and second in rushing yards (career highs in both). He finished 10th among quarterbacks in fantasy points, but that's a bit misleading, as his inconsistent production led to five top-five weeks but no other finishes better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and 15th in fantasy points per game in each of the past four seasons, though it's fair to expect a leap forward in 2026 with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater healthy and a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel. Herbert is safest as a QB2, but there's upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Jefferson will look to keep it rolling in Week 2 as Minnesota takes on the Bears. Jefferson returned to a fantasy level in Week 1 that he didn't see much of in 2025, reeling in eight of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The star wideout also had a solid connection with veteran Carson Wentz, who came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion). Given that Jefferson still produced with the Vikings' QB2, he could be in line for big games no matter who lines up under center, so long as it isn't J.J. McCarthy. He'll face a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Jefferson will look to rebound from a quieter week as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jefferson was held to three catches for 55 yards against the Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in bad weather and ended with a 9-3 score. The superstar pass catcher has 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he could increase those numbers twofold against a Bucs defense that ceded 95 yards and a touchdown to Cleveland receiver Denzel Boston this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Jefferson will look to return as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jefferson exited Week 3 against the Buccaneers with an ankle injury, but there don't appear to be any concerns beyond a sprain at this point. The star wideout has totaled 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season even in just five halves, and he's been a major piece of Minnesota's 3-0 start. If he is healthy, Jefferson will face a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Jefferson will aim to make a return for Minnesota's Week 5 clash at New Orleans. Jefferson sat out of the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins with an ankle injury, but the hope is that his absences will be limited to that game. The star pass catcher has totaled a quieter 13-179-2 receiving line over his first two-plus games, so he'll look to make a bang if he does return to action. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season, which could provide everything Jefferson needs to deliver.

player.seasonOutlook: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns aren't fully solved, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to work as the starter. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey McBride enters Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit coming off his quietest performance of the season. While the star tight end logged a healthy 12 targets and seven catches against the Giants in Week 4, he finished with just 31 receiving yards. It's a testament to McBride's excellence that such a stat line represents a downturn by his standards, and he'll have a good chance of bouncing back against the Lions. Detroit has allowed a whopping 19.2 fantasy points per game to tight ends so far this season, by far the most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: CeeDee Lamb is coming off a game for the ages. Lamb was targeted a staggering 21 times en route to an absurd 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown in the comeback win over the Texans. It was the third-straight 100-yard outing of the season for Lamb, and he scored for the fourth time in four contests. Following this outing, Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards and receptions, and is tied for third in the NFL with four receiving scores. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxson Dart was electric in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for an additional 54 yards in the stunning 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Dart threw just five incompletions and showed excellent rapport with new tight end Isaiah Likely. Dart was accurate, decisive and poised in what amounted to an extremely promising start to the season for the G-Men. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Los Angeles Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in their opener, allowing 379 scrimmage yards, which ranks them in the bottom third of the NFL. The Rams were torched on the ground in particular to the tune of 174 yards. While Myles Garrett will be sidelined due to a knee injury, the Rams will get Aaron Donald back from retirement when they host the Giants on Monday Night Football.

player.seasonOutlook: Dart is a strong 2026 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie campaign in which he delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for fifth most) despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. Dart was solid as a passer but elite as a rusher, finishing in the top five at the position in rushing attempts, yards, TDs and carries inside the 5-yard line. Dart's aggressive playing style raises concerns about his durability, but it also provides the 23-year-old with elite fantasy upside. With a new coaching staff led by John Harbaugh and a new playcaller in Matt Nagy, as well as an improved supporting cast that includes a healthy Malik Nabers and newcomers Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney, Dart is best valued as a midrange QB1 with a high ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Goodson is the third backup running back already for the Cowboys this season. With Malik Davis injured and Emari Demercado deemed ineffective, Goodson had six carries for 22 yards in his season-debut versus the Ravens. However, Javonte Williams remains the undisputed starter, leaving Goodson and company picking up the scraps. In Week 4, the Cowboys will also face a rather stingy Texans run defense allowing 86.7 yards per game on the ground, which is fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Goodson managed three carries for 12 yards last game for the Cowboys. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams had 24 touches and three touchdowns in the comeback win over the Texans. In other words, Goodson's utility is extremely low barring injury. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Patriots in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. He caught three of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory versus Atlanta. Wilson tied for second on the team in targets and was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps. Despite the solid start, it's best he remains on benches or waiver wires until he can prove to be a consistent fantasy contributor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Roman Wilson and the Steelers welcome the division rival Bengals to town for a Week 3 matchup. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, Wilson stepped into the No. 2 receiver role behind DK Metcalf. He finished the 20-3 loss with a team-high five catches for 28 yards on six targets. Rookie Germie Bernard was one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite receivers, however, turning eight targets into four catches and a team-leading 35 yards. Pittman's status is cloudy at best for Week 3, but Wilson and the Steelers face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs, so he's best left on benches for now.
outlooksByWeek.4: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 4. He caught three of six targets for 60 yards and his first touchdown of the season during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Wilson led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished second behind Darnell Washington in yardage. He has a favorable matchup versus Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs, but it's still difficult to trust him with so many mouths to feed in the Steelers' offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Roman Wilson and the Steelers take on the Colts at home in Week 5. He caught three of six targets for 74 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Wilson tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage, and he now has a TD catch in two consecutive contests. He's been a reliable option for Aaron Rodgers, as he's generated six targets in all four outings this season en route to a 14-188-2 line. Wilson's next opportunity comes against the Colts' 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Blake Corum will aim to rebound from a pair of quiet games when the Rams host the Bills in Week 5. After after averaging 66.5 rushing yards in Los Angeles' first two games, Corum has totaled just 29 yards on the ground over his past two contests. He's been quite inefficient with his carries, logging just 2.6 yards per carry on his 11 totes while Kyren Williams has dominated backfield touches. Buffalo has given up six TDs to running backs this season, but three have come through the air. That's not Corum's forte -- he has just four catches for 20 yards with no scores as a receiver through four weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more effective as the Packers play the Jets in Week 2. While Lloyd was the leading rusher for Green Bay in Week 1, he still only totaled 37 yards on 13 rushing attempts. Fellow ball carrier Chris Brooks also recorded seven carries for 29 yards, so the margin between the two doesn't appear to be too large. Lloyd will look to do more with his opportunities against a New York front that should be less menacing than Minnesota's.
outlooksByWeek.3: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more efficient as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Lloyd scored his first career touchdown off a six-yard catch in Week 2, but he also rushed six times for just 20 yards. The inexperienced running back has now averaged just 3.0 YPC off 19 carries this season, which is far from what Green Bay is looking for out of its RB1. Lloyd will also face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a top-10 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make his job even harder.
outlooksByWeek.4: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to turn things around as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Lloyd continued his disappointing season against the Falcons in Week 3, rushing four times for 11 yards and catching two of three passes for seven yards. While the inexperienced running back was hindered by a pass-heavy game script, he's still averaged just three yards per carry across 23 attempts and seen his offensive snap share decrease in each of his first three games. He'll also face a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs this year, making him a very risky play.
outlooksByWeek.5: MarShawn Lloyd remains in the mix of Green Bay's backfield ahead of Week 5 against Chicago. Lloyd remained extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 4, rushing the ball seven times for 13 yards, but he did salvage his performance with five catches for 36 yards. The second-year running back looks to be in direct competition with Kaleb Johnson for carries as of late, but the Packers have utilized Lloyd in different ways even when Johnson has been more effective. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed (4.73) to RBs this season, which could give Lloyd the opening he needs to do more as a rusher.

player.seasonOutlook: Due to a variety of injuries, Lloyd has appeared in one game since being selected in the third round of the 2024 draft. Now healthy, he appears to have a hold on No. 2 RB duties in Green Bay, which is notable with Josh Jacobs facing a potential suspension. Lloyd is likely to open the season on the RB2/flex radar and should be on your radar in the middle rounds, though note that he'll fade back to no more than an insurance stash once Jacobs returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Myers will look to remain perfect this season when the Seahawks visit Arizona in Week 2. Myers made his lone PAT try and both field-goal attempts in a season-opening win over New England, though his FGs were relative chip shots from 30 and 26 yards. Myers made nine field goals from 50-plus yards out each of the previous two seasons, however, so he has plenty of leg to convert from that distance when called upon. The Cardinals aren't expected to be a top NFL defense this year, but they performed well in limiting the Chargers to 14 points in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Myers has provided Seattle with a steady boot this season heading into a Week 3 matchup against Washington. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field-goal tries and all five of his PAT attempts through two weeks. However, he hasn't yet been asked to hit from distance, as none of his FG tries have been from 40 yards or greater. The Commanders have yielded a whopping 30.5 points per game through two weeks, so Myers could get plenty of opportunities to kick in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Myers enters Seattle's Week 4 clash against the Chargers having not missed a kick so far this season. Myers handled only relatively short kicks over his first two games, but he showed off his leg with a 57-yard field goal against Washington in Week 3. The veteran kicker is now 4-for-4 on FG tries and 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts this season. Opponents have gone 6-for-7 on field-goal attempts against the Chargers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Myers has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle on tap to host San Francisco in Week 5. After attempting a career-high 48 field goals in 2025, Myers has had just five FG tries so far this season, making all of them. He's been more active kicking extra points, making 12 of 13 PATs. Perhaps Myers will be relied upon more versus the 49ers, who have allowed just five extra-point tries as opposed to nine FG attempts so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian Watson will remain a top option in Green Bay's passing game against the Bears in Week 5. Watson finished Week 4 at Tampa Bay with a quiet three catches for 47 yards, but Jordan Love threw for just 197 yards. The go-to wideout has now posted a 20-331-4 receiving line on 32 targets so far this campaign, and he's on pace for his first 1,000-yard season if he can stay healthy. Watson could have a tough task versus a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Terry McLaurin missed last game for the Commanders due to a hamstring injury. McLaurin allegedly pushed hard to play, though, meaning he could very well return to the field in Week 5 versus the Giants. He also could have his starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. New York has been stingy against the pass in 2026 thus far, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. Likewise, the G-Men are tied for the league-lead with six picks.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games.
