His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards last game for the Eagles. Philadelphia fell behind in the second half, though, which forced the Eagles to all but abandon the run. Barkley has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season. In Week 4, Barkley will face a stout defensive line with Aaron Donald when the Eagles clash with the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Bowers made up for lost time after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from minor knee surgery. In his Week 3 season debut against the Saints, the star tight end turned 13 targets into a 10-116-1 receiving line. Bowers is the clear No. 1 downfield option for Kirk Cousins, especially considering the lack of talent in the wide receiver room, and as long as he can stay healthy, he should continue to see big volume. He's in a good position to put up big numbers again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs but ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Bowers shook off an illness to once again be the Raiders' top receiving option in a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. He caught six of 11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, finding the end zone for a second straight game after missing the first two weeks of the year while completing his recovery from knee surgery. The star tight end is the most dangerous weapon in Kirk Cousins' arsenal, and he's likely to continue getting double-digit targets on a weekly basis while posting elite numbers. Bowers faces his toughest test of the season so far in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Purdy will look to help keep San Francisco's perfect record alive with a win over Seattle in Week 5. Purdy has been outstanding to the begin the campaign, completing 70% of his passes and recording an 11:1 TD:INT. He's also getting great protection from the offensive line, as he's yet to take a sack this season. The Seahawks could pose a stiff challenge, however, as they've collected seven sacks through five games and have allowed the fifth-lowest passer rating (76.2) in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dontayvion Wicks made his presence felt in his Eagles debut in Week 1. Wicks reeled in two passes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the 24-22 win over Washington. Only Dallas Goedert had more receiving yards than Wicks for the game. Wicks also notched four targets in his premiere for the Birds. In Week 2, Wicks will face a dismal Titans defense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing scores a season ago, which was tied for 23rd in the NFL
outlooksByWeek.3: Dontayvion Wicks continues to cement himself as the No. 2 wideout in the Eagles offense. Wicks caught five passes for 74 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Wicks was second on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury, and with Dallas Goedert also banged up, Wicks could be one of the chief beneficiaries.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dontayvion Wicks had his first subpar game of the season for the Eagles. Wicks had five targets but caught just two passes for 32 yards in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Wicks had a crucial drop en route to being held under 73 yards receiving for the first time in 2026. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dontayvion Wicks was expected to operate as the No. 1 wideout for the Eagles last game due to the injury to DeVonta Smith. Unfortunately, Philadelphia's offense was stymied, and Wicks managed three catches for just 18 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Smith appears unlikely to play in Week 5 versus the Jags, so Wicks should continue to play a prominent role in the offense. However, it was Darius Cooper who scored twice last game, and rookie Makai Lemon outpaced Wicks in both targets as well as receiving yards. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre' Harris is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but he's been Justin Herbert's most reliable option, topping 50 receiving yards in each of the Chargers' last three games. Harris has put together a 13-209-0 line on 21 targets over four weeks, and he could make a push for the top spot on the WR depth chart with Ladd McConkey now dealing with both rib and foot injuries and Quentin Johnston failing to do much with his opportunities. Harris will aim for his first trip to the end zone in 2026 in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.4: Jalon Daniels is set to start in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Tampa Bay's Week 4 matchup against the Packers. In three preseason games, the undrafted rookie from Kansas accounted for 276 total yards and two touchdowns while turning the ball over just once. In college, Daniels showed incredible arm talent and scrambling ability, though he struggled with accuracy at times. He's in for a tough matchup in his first NFL start, as the Packers' defense has allowed just 18.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalon Daniels is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Daniels struggled during his first NFL start in Week 4, throwing for 148 yards, two interceptions and a touchdown while adding 55 yards on the ground. However, he showed flashes of potential and could take advantage of a Cowboys defense that's allowing 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Daniels could really thrive getting out of the pocket, as Dallas' defense has given up the most rushing yards to quarterbacks (188) in the NFL through four games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keaton Mitchell could be moving into a bigger role in the Chargers' backfield. While the offense as a whole is struggling, the former Raven logged a season-high eight carries in Week 3 and turned them into 52 rushing yards. He also made his first trip to the end zone in 2026, getting a one-yard shovel pass from Justin Herbert on a jet sweep. Omarion Hampton is struggling to adapt to new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and that's opening the door for Mitchell to push his way into a timeshare in the backfield. However, neither back is likely to make a splash in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keaton Mitchell's role in the Chargers' backfield continues to grow. The former Raven handled a season-high 15 touches in a Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, turning them into 63 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton produced 53 yards and a rushing TD on 11 touches, and Kimani Vidal added 36 yards and a receiving score on seven touches. That split points toward offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel moving into a full-blown backfield committee, and while Mitchell's volume has been trending up, he hasn't done much yet to make a case for the No. 1 spot on the depth chart. He'll look to make his own trip to the end zone in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. One week after leading the team in yardage while finishing second in targets, Bernard fell victim to a Steelers offense that prefers to spread the ball around, as Aaron Rodgers completed passes to nine different receivers in the win. Cleveland's defense is susceptible through the air, as they're tied for 29th in receiving TDs allowed (5) through three games, but Bernard is off the fantasy radar for now.
outlooksByWeek.5: Germie Bernard and the Steelers return home to square off against the Colts in Week 5. The rookie wideout caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Bernard should remain on fantasy benches while playing behind veterans DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, and Jaylen Warren, along with tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. Indianapolis allows 35.0 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 20th, but his limited involvement on offense doesn't inspire much confidence.

player.seasonOutlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third or fourth in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf and perhaps Roman Wilson. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury to help the Dolphins against the Bengals in Week 5. He missed the last two weeks, and his role in this low-volume passing offense is questionable; he drew seven targets in Week 1 and only three in Week 2. The Bengals defense is much improved and ranks 14th in points allowed to opposing wideouts, with no receiver topping 63 yards against them. While Douglas can stretch the field, availability and usage remain question marks.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Washington's volume was limited in his NFL debut, but he was productive, gaining 41 rushing yards on seven carries in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins. The quality of his opposition needs to be taken into account, but it was still a strong showing from the 2026 fourth-round pick. Lead back Ashton Jeanty had a huge game, proving he was fully recovered from a preseason ankle injury, but if he has trouble staying on the field, Washington appears very capable of stepping into a larger role. He'll face a tough matchup in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't logged big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Washington failed to produce another big play in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, managing only 18 rushing yards on nine carries while catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground, but Washington hasn't yet shown enough consistency to be any kind of threat to his workload on early downs. The rookie is averaging 5.0 yards on his first 24 NFL carries, though, well clear of Jeanty's 3.4 mark, so volume could begin to tilt his way a little more if that trend continues. Washington will try to break free in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Mevis is coming off a quiet season opener as the Rams prepare to face the Giants in Week 2. Los Angeles' offense was held by the 49ers to just seven points last Thursday, and Mevis didn't get the opportunity to attempt any field goals. The Rams figure to be much more prolific on that side of the ball most weeks, so Mevis should be more active moving forward, though last year he attempted 39 PATs to just 13 field goals. The Giants' defense put up a good performance in a Week 1 win over Dallas, with star kicker Brandon Aubrey getting no field-goal tries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Mevis is still searching for his first field-goal conversion heading into the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Mevis didn't try a FG in Week 1, and he missed his only attempt -- a 43-yarder -- on Monday Night Football. Mevis did make all four of his extra-point tries and figures to kick a lot of those given the Rams' explosive offense. Kickers have gone 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts against the Broncos so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Mevis is coming off a career-best four FGs ahead of the Rams' matchup versus Philadelphia in Week 4. After going 0-for-1 in field-goal tries over the first two weeks of the campaign, Mevis was asked to attempt four FGs versus Denver in Week 3 and made every try, including a 48-yarder. With that said, the Rams' explosive offense doesn't frequently end drives with field-goal attempts, so Mevis may struggle to see such volume moving forward. Opponents have been successful on five of six field-goal attempts versus the Eagles so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harrison Mevis heads into the Rams' Week 5 matchup against Buffalo with a modest four field goals on the season. Four of those came in Week 3 against Denver, and Mevis missed a 48-yard try this past Sunday against Philadelphia. The second-year pro is a perfect 10-for-10 on point-after tries this year and has made all 49 of his PAT attempts in his career. Buffalo has yielded just six FG tries through four weeks, with kickers making five of those attempts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malachi Fields scored his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. The rookie flashed his big-play ability, snagging a 40-yarder from quarterback Jameis Winston along with the 12-yard score. He finished with two catches for a career-best 52 yards and the touchdown. In Week 5, Fields and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches on offense to be worth considering in fantasy against Denver's stout defense in Week 2. He had one target and one carry in Jacksonville's season opener, which he turned into 11 scrimmage yards across four snaps on offense while playing primarily on defense. Hunter played both wide receiver and cornerback at Colorado before being drafted second overall by the Jaguars in 2025. With WRs Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers ahead of him, the versatile Hunter is currently more useful to the Jaguars on defense, much to the chagrin of his fantasy managers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Hunter didn't have a target or carry in Week 2 and has played only a handful of snaps on offense for the Jaguars this season. He's off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, outside of IDP formats that reward Hunter's contributions as a cornerback. Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers should continue to lead Jacksonville's wide receiver room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense in either of Jacksonville's last two games heading into a Week 4 trip to Cincinnati. The 2025 second overall pick has been playing almost exclusively on defense, so Hunter's off the fantasy radar in formats that don't count individual defensive statistics. He's trending up as a cornerback after intercepting Drake Maye in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots.
outlooksByWeek.5: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense for the Jaguars since Week 1. He played every defensive snap in Week 4 and is focusing primarily on playing cornerback rather than wide receiver. Hunter is a fantasy non-factor except in formats that reward his defensive contributions. Jacksonville will face the Eagles in Week 5 in London, where Hunter showcased his upside on offense last season with eight catches for 101 yards and a TD against the Rams. Don't expect a repeat performance anytime soon, if ever.

player.seasonOutlook: Full-time focus on defense should unlock rewarding production from a unique talent. Not only can Hunter mirror receivers, he frequently turns his head to track the ball, leading to big plays in coverage.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam Darnold suffered a soft-tissue glute injury in Seattle's season-opening win and isn't likely to play in Week 2 against Arizona. As a result, Drew Lock is in line to guide the Seahawks' offense. Darnold isn't expected to miss significant time and could be back as soon as Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam Darnold has a chance to return from a glute injury for Seattle's Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. It remains to be seen if the veteran QB will be able to suit up, but he reportedly has been ahead of schedule in his recovery. With Darnold out against Arizona in Week 2, Drew Lock took over and led the Seahawks to a win. Whichever signal-caller starts under center in Week 3 could feast upon a Washington defense that has allowed a 137.0 passer rating this season, the worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam Darnold seems to be past the glute injury that cost him some early-season action heading into Seattle's Week 4 tilt against the Chargers. Darnold returned from a one-week absence to throw for 379 yards and four touchdowns (albeit with two interceptions) in a Week 3 win against Washington. The veteran QB continued to look often to star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who logged a massive 10-128-2 receiving line on 14 targets. The Chargers have given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, 11th-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam Darnold will look to lead Seattle to victory in a key NFC West clash versus San Francisco in Week 5. Darnold threw for a modest 168 yards and was picked off once against the Chargers in Week 4, but he tossed two touchdowns and guided his team to a win. After playing only five snaps over the first two weeks due to a glute injury, Darnold looks to be back to full health and has posted a 6:3 TD:INT over the Seahawks' past two games. He could face a stiff challenge against the 49ers, who have yielded only three passing TDs through four weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Darnold's first season with the Super Bowl champion Seahawks couldn't have gone much better from a real-life standpoint, but it simply didn't translate to much fantasy success. Despite finishing fifth in the NFL in passing yards for the second season in a row, Darnold finished 27th in fantasy points per game. He was very boom or bust, delivering seven top-10 weeks but also nine finishes outside the top 20. Turnovers (15 INTs were second most in the NFL) and a lack of rushing were the culprits. The 29-year-old will have a new playcaller in Brian Fleury, but otherwise it's roughly the status quo offensively. Darnold is no more than a fringe QB2 with a limited ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive.
