He next draws a juicy matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points per game (32.7) to quarterbacks on the campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 2 matchup versus Miami on the heels of making two field goals in San Francisco's season-opening victory against the Rams. Pineiro's makes came from 20 and 56 yards out, though he also missed a 52-yarder. The veteran kicker made a career-high six FGs from 50-plus yards out last year, so San Francisco is clearly comfortable relying on his leg from that distance. The 49ers could put up plenty of points in Week 2, as the Dolphins just gave up 27 points to Las Vegas in a Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Eddy Pineiro remains a solid fantasy kicker option heading into the 49ers' Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal Sunday against the Dolphins, but he converted all five of his extra-point tries. San Francisco has averaged 31.0 points per game through two weeks, so Pineiro figures to see frequent opportunities to kick, though that won't always result in field-goal chances. Arizona's opponents have attempted just one FG through two weeks, but the Cardinals gave up a hefty 31 points to Seattle in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Eddy Pineiro will look to get his consistency back on track for San Francisco in Week 4 versus the Broncos. Pineiro missed a pair of extra-point tries Sunday in a win over Arizona, but he also nailed a 57-yard field goal. The veteran kicker hadn't previously struggled with PATs, making all eight over his first two games of the campaign, so his erratic boot may have just been an aberration. Denver has yielded eight field-goal attempts and seven extra-point tries through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Eddy Pineiro's leg could be key for the 49ers in Week 5 versus Seattle in a battle of tough defenses. Pineiro has been mostly asked to kick extra points this season, making 14 of 16 PAT tries while attempting just six field goals (and making four of them). He missed a 54-yard try against Denver this past Sunday, though it was blocked by the Broncos. There may not be many opportunities for Pineiro against the Seahawks, who are giving up the fifth-fewest points (18.3) in the league this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the Falcons for a Week 5 showdown. He rushed once for three yards and caught two of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Derrick Henry out-carried Hill 23-1, even with Lamar Jackson missing the entire second half with an ankle injury. It appears that regardless of who's under center, the Ravens' backfield belongs to Henry. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against an Atlanta defense allowing just 17.9 points per game to RBs, which ranks ninth.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals in Week 2. Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in a season-opening win against New England, though he would have had a bigger performance if not for a 24-yard touchdown grab that was nullified by a penalty. Of note, Drew Lock is expected to start behind center for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with a glute injury and is unlikely to suit up. The Cardinals aren't expected to field a top secondary this year, but they did a good job of holding Justin Herbert and the Chargers' offense in check in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cooper Kupp will look to rebound from a quiet performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Against the Chargers this past Sunday, Kupp caught just one of two targets for 13 yards. It was his lowest offensive output of the season, though he's been pretty quiet overall with two or fewer receptions in three of four contests so far. The 49ers are yielding just 123.5 receiving yards per game to wideouts, seventh-fewest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley wasn't targeted in Tennessee's season opener and is off the fantasy radar completely heading into a Week 2 home game against the elite Eagles secondary. The veteran WR may be as low as fifth in the Titans' WR pecking order behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike. Second-year QB Cam Ward has struggled to keep any of his pass catchers consistently fantasy-relevant, let alone depth options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.
outlooksByWeek.5: Calvin Ridley has just three catches for 48 yards on five targets through four games. He's barely contributing as the No. 4 WR in a Titans offense that's averaging just 13.8 points per game, which is the second-fewest in the NFL. Even in a Week 5 matchup against a Texans defense that has struggled to defend wide receivers, Ridley remains a non-factor in fantasy.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance. The lost season comes after Ridley delivered consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, finishing both as a top-30 fantasy receiver. Ridley is now 31 years old and has added target competition with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson in the mix. A Year 2 leap from Cam Ward could get Ridley back into the flex discussion, but it's more likely that he's headed for a reduced role. Ridley is worth no more than a middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

Singleton was selected by the Titans in the fifth round of April's draft. He is a big, versatile back with terrific speed who can contribute as a rusher, receiver, blocker and returner. While working in a committee with fellow rookie Kaytron Allen at Penn State the past four years, Singleton was effective after contact (3.46 YAC is sixth best in this RB rookie class) but struggled with elusiveness (8.0 forced missed tackle rate is worst). He was solid as receiver (102-987-9) and returner (class-high 1,138 kick return yards) during his 53-game tenure. Singleton will open his career behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, but would make for an interesting waiver add in the event of a Pollard injury.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenyon Sadiq could have an emerging role for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Sadiq notched four touches in his NFL debut, including a three-yard rushing score, out-gaining starter Mason Taylor handsomely in a run-heavy game for the Jets. They'll likely need to throw more to keep up with Green Bay's offense in Week 2, and the Packers allowed a touchdown to a tight end last week. The floor is volatile, but Sadiq offers high ceiling potential for those in need at tight end.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenyon Sadiq could struggle to build on a breakout performance in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. After recording just six targets in his first two games, Sadiq shined in Week 3, catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, despite playing just 56% of the offensive snaps in Mason Taylor's absence. The Bears have not allowed an opposing tight end to top 30 yards this season, with teams finding more success targeting their corners, so a repeat performance may be challenging.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenyon Sadiq faces an unsettled role in the Jets' limited passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. After a Week 3 breakthrough performance, Sadiq failed to record a catch on four targets in Week 4 and now has 21 or fewer yards in three of his first four games. The Browns haven't allowed an opposing tight end to top 51 yards while surrendering just 6.7 yards per target, not boding well for Sadiq in Week 5. A potential Mason Taylor return would further dampen Sadiq's potential.

player.seasonOutlook: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.

outlooksByWeek.2: Braelon Allen will look to build on a solid opener when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Braelon Allen could be slated for bulk carries in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns with Breece Hall's (quad) uncertain availability. Filling in for Hall in Week 4, Allen was the only Jet to receive a carry, putting him in line to potentially exploit a Cleveland defense that's allowed at least 82 yards to opposing lead backs in three straight weeks and an appealing 4.8 yards per carry. If Hall returns, he can't be guaranteed a full workload, lending flex appeal to Allen.

player.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Penix will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Penix has been great through two starts in 2026, throwing for 479 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He's helped rejuvenate Atlanta's offense, as the team has scored a whopping 40 points per game since his return. Despite this, Penix is in for a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 18.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
outlooksByWeek.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.
outlooksByWeek.5: TreVeyon Henderson will seek chunk plays in the Patriots' Week 5 matchup against a vulnerable Raiders run defense. Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Thomas has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last two games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances.
