He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Courtland Sutton was nearly invisible in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, catching only one of six targets for a measly four yards. The veteran wideout remains firmly behind Jaylen Waddle on the depth chart, but the entire Denver offense is struggling under first-time play caller Davis Webb, and Sutton has produced a weak 9-86-0 line on 22 targets through four games. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming play-calling duties is an open question. Sutton will try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield is set for a difficult Week 3 matchup when the Buccaneers take on the Vikings, whose defense has allowed 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Mayfield has really struggled during Tampa Bay's first two contests, accounting for just two touchdowns while turning the ball over four times. He's thrown for just 184.5 passing yards per game while completing 71 percent of his passes. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 3 matchup, with Minnesota's defense giving up just 12.5 points per game this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Harrison heads into Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit struggling to build chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. Though Harrison recorded a 12-yard touchdown reception in Week 4 against the Giants, that was his only catch on four targets. The third-year wideout has exceeded one reception just once through four games this season and has totaled only 12 targets, remarkably far behind the 44 targets fellow wideout Michael Wilson has logged. With that said, the Lions could provide a prime opportunity for Harrison to get back on track, as Detroit has surrendered 207.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, third-worst in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a disappointing start in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite Michael Penix returning to the field in the Week 3 win over the Packers, Pitts' role remained limited, catching just one of two targets for five yards. He was overshadowed by Drake London (9-194-0) and appears to be operating as the Falcons' No. 3 pass catcher, also behind Bijan Robinson (16 targets to Pitts' six). However, Pitts could rebound in Week 4, as the Saints' defense has allowed 20.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Pitts had his most productive game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 47 yards. Despite this, he played just 50% of Atlanta's offensive snaps and has now logged an average of 2.3 targets per game, suggesting he may not be as involved in the team's offensive game plan as he has been in past years. Additionally, Pitts in in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 10.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.
